sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL  ON THE 10 th OF JULY, 2025  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 20238 of 2025  BALRAM PANDEY  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:
Shri Vipul Pathak - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Sukhendra Kushwaha with Shri Vipin Kumar Bari - Ad  complainant/Objector.
Shri C.M. Tiwari - Government Advocate for the responde

ORDER This is the second application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.306/2024 registered at Police Station Sanjeevani Nagar, District Jabalpur (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B, 34 of I.P.C. & 339-A, 339-B, 339-C,
339-D, 339-E, 339-F of M.P. Municipalities Act, 1961.
The applicant is in custody since 24.09.2024.

First application was dismissed as withdrawn.
2.

As per the First Information Report, complainants Rakesh Kumar Kushwaha, Pradeep Patel,
Ravishankar Namdev, Radha Kushwaha, Kailash Prasad Dahiya, Ajay Kachhi, Om Prakash Patel &
Bhanupratap Patel have given a complaint to Sanjeevani Nagar police station that the accused/applicant was owner of land Khasra number 96/1/1, area 0.292 hectare (31419 sq. ft.) but he had sold more than 22550 sq. ft. of the land to the above mentioned complainants and they neither got any possession of the land nor their name was transferred in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30819 2 MCRC-20238-2025 revenue records.
The accused/applicant prepared a rough layout and sold it without the permission of TNCP/Municipal Corporation and has cheated people by selling the same plot more than twice.
Therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent.
He is in custody since 24.09.2024.
It is submitted that two cases cannot be set in motion on the same step.
It is submitted that one criminal case was lodged in the year 2020 by Nilesh Rai against the applicant.

sentences.text: 1 submitted that in this case land was purchased by Abhishek Tiwari from Summi Bai and the sale deed of the plot was executed by Abhishek Tiwari.
It is also submitted that only Kailash Dahiya has deposed against the present applicant and he has received the money from the account of Kailash Dahiya.

It is submitted that as per statement of complainant Rs.
4,70,000/- was paid in the account of applicant whereas bank statement of the applicant shows that Rs. 4,87,000/- was deposited in his account.
There is no evidence of receiving Rs. 2,90,000/-.

It is also submitted that in this case agreement was executed between both the parties, although, Kailash Dahiya has denied the execution of agreement but that denial does not affect the execution of agreement.

He has placed reliance on Naresh Kumar and another Vs. State of Karnataka, 2024 SCC Online SC 268, T.T. Antony Vs. State of Kerala and others, (2001) 6 SCC (Cri) 1048, International Advanced Research Centre for Powder Metallurgy and New Materials (ARCI) and others Vs. Nimra Cerglass Technics Private Limited and anothers, (2016) 1 SCC 348.

sentences.text: Charge sheet has been filed and the conclusion of trial will take considerable time.
Hence, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Objector/complainants as well NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30819 3 MCRC-20238-2025 as counsel for the State have opposed the bail application and have submitted that present applicant is also one of the main accused.
Co-accused Abhishek Tiwari was the employee of present applicant and accused Samrat Pandey and he was performing the work under their guidance.
Kailash Dahiya has given cheque of Rs. 5,00,000/- to the present applicant and money has also come in the account of present applicant.
Other witnesses have also stated against the applicant.
He has actively participated in the offence and total 38 sale deeds have been executed by the present applicant and other co-accused and several persons have been cheated by them.
There are five criminal antecedents of the applicant for the same nature of offence.
Hence, the applicant do not deserve grant of bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case as well as seriousness of the offence, I am not inclined to grant regular bail to the applicant.
7. Accordingly, present MCRC stands dismissed.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE navin Balram Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192690814/
